acceptance: A decision record identifies the supported user outcome, current callers, canonical ETL capabilities, and any concrete gap that requires separate scheduling.
If retained, every submitted task maps to a real transform with defined inputs, outputs, idempotency, failure semantics, and parity tests against the canonical ETL path.
If rebuilt, benchmark evidence demonstrates why the canonical path cannot meet the requirement and defines a maintenance owner and performance budget.

If deprecated or removed, the change names an owner, deprecation and removal versions, at least one beta compatibility cycle where applicable, migration instructions, and corrected deployment-guide examples.
The documented TPC-DI parallel API decision is reconciled with decide-fate-of-documented-unimplemented-surfaces; its other two surfaces remain untouched.
No placeholder or synthetic task may enter production data mutation under any selected outcome.
context: The smallest likely solution is to reuse the canonical ETL orchestration or remove the extra surface. A new scheduler needs affirmative evidence, not feature-completeness preference.
description:
After false-success containment, decide whether the enhanced TPC-DI parallel feature has a supported product role. The repository already has a canonical ETL path and a broad open tracker item about a documented but nonexistent public parallel API. Avoid sustaining a second scheduler without a demonstrated requirement.

Decision boundary: choose exactly one outcome: route the public feature to canonical real transforms; rebuild a distinct scheduler only when a measured capability gap cannot be met by the canonical path; or deprecate and remove the enhanced surface. The decision must resolve the TPC-DI portion of decide-fate-of-documented-unimplemented-surfaces without changing that item's unrelated admin and explorer scopes.
